trial_court: Principal District & Sessions Judge, Davanagere in S.C.No.34/2011
case_name: Smt. M. Bhagyamma vs M. C. Rajendra

parties.respondent_defendant: M. C. Rajendra and others (husband, father-in-law, mother-in-law, brother-in-law)

facts_of_case: The complainant's husband and his family members were prosecuted for offences punishable under Sections 498A and 307 read with Section 34 of IPC and Sections 3 & 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961. The trial court acquitted them. This appeal challenges that order.

legal_principles.principle: In an appeal against the order of acquittal, the Appellate Court shall be slow in interfering with the judgment of acquittal.
legal_principles.held: It is settled principle of law that in an appeal against the order of acquittal, the Appellate Court shall be slow in interfering with the judgment of acquittal.

legal_principles.principle: Unless the order of acquittal suffers patent illegality or perversity, the Appellate Court cannot interfere with the same merely on the ground that another view is probable.
legal_principles.held: It is settled law that unless the order of acquittal suffers patent illegality or perversity, the Appellate Court cannot interfere with the same merely on the ground that another view is probable.

outcome.final_order: The judgment dated 17.10.2015 passed by the Principal District & Sessions Judge, Davanagere in S.C.No.34/2011 is upheld.
